Episode 247. Liberation War of Lafrarosa (11)
Hmph, are you saying it's like right now, Lokia?]
[In some ways, it is. From now on, you have to protect Lafrarosa against this tremendous war machine. But let me tell you something, descendant.]
The word 'descendant' had barely left his lips when Jin unleashed a strike. A sharp flash of blue light tore through the red protective shield between the air fortresses and penetrated inside.
Swoosh!
The massive screen displaying Lokia's face shattered.
"How dare you call me a descendant. Are you deaf? Or do you think, appearing as a spirit, you are invincible?"
Jin had realized that Lokia's presence was just a projection, not his real body. The fusion with the Battle God, which Lokia kept trying to sever, was now even more strongly bonded.
[...Oh, if I were still my former self. That strike just now would have been quite chilling.]
"Then it means the former you had better senses. For the first and last time, I will give you a chance. Leave. Today is the only moment you can meet me and still be safe."
A deep and majestic voice resounded, causing Lokia to shudder for a moment at the vibrations transmitted across the ship.
Perhaps Murakan's words were right, he thought first.

[But it's been too long since I got nervous about such words. I'm too worn out to feel fear. Haha, alright. I'll stop calling you a descendant. After all, I've decided not to dwell on the current generation of swordsmen anymore.]

"Current generation of swordsmen, huh. We've confirmed that you've formed a void space, creating a kind of world. You say you have no lingering attachment to Runcandel, but my worthless kin are participating in your little game there, aren't they? Joshua, Myu, and Anne."
Jin felt it.
Lokia was certainly feeling regret. The children from Runcandel she brought to nurture her own world were nothing but pitiful losers.
"The brightest of the clan are all with me, Lokia. Have you ever wondered why you couldn’t take even one of them?"
[Haha, what is it?]

"It's because you didn't endure. There might have been a time when you sacrificed for the clan, but that's all. In the end, you chose betrayal instead of enduring, fighting, and struggling together. And yet, you act as if you're a creator, trying to remake the world just to have Runcandel. It's nothing but an ugly obsession."

Jin had never seen Lokia's world directly and didn't know exactly what it was. However, it was clear that Lokia coveted 'Runcandel'. It was an obsession with Runcandel that glittered in his eyes beyond the giant screen.
"However, the only thing you can take from my Runcandel is just one, Lokia Ganesto. That is the punishment you deserve."

-[He was a traitor... colluding with the witch, turning Temar into a monster. It was all Lokia's scheme. The temporary departure of Solderet from Temar, the betrayal of the gods, even the rise of Zipfel.]
-Tell me more in detail.

-[Before killing me, Lokia said his goal was the resurrection of the Sun God. That's why he killed all his comrades and only spared Bale. He wanted to erase the current world and reclaim a righteous one. Something about the world's original form, Lokia used everything for that. The clan, the witch, even Zipfel.]
Jin recalled the words Padler uttered like a last will before his disappearance. The deeds of Lokia were unforgivable, regardless of what lay behind them.
"Lokia Ganesto!"
Blue thunder energy formed in Jin's eyes.

"You betrayed the clan a thousand years ago, harmed Temar Runcandel and the Ten Knights, those who followed them, and have continued that cursed life to plot against the clan to this day. As the head of the clan, I'll tell you the punishment you deserve. The punishment is eternal despair. You won't be able to achieve what you desire, possess what you want, or reach what you long for."
Whoosh! Sizzle...
The fierce thunder energy of the Plutonian Domination Sword once again filled the great desert. In less than a second, the chaotic energy encroaching near Jin was pushed back.
A blue storm, centered around Jin, formed a semicircle and moved endlessly forward.
The four air fortresses were pushed back by its force all the way behind Kri, and Shimat, who had been wandering in the pit, rose to the surface and gripped his sword.
'What is this... It's not over yet?'
Like mist clearing, Shimat's dark eyes, shrouded in despair, opened.

He felt as if he had finally emerged from a cave into the light. This blue thunder energy, though powerful enough to tear him apart, more brutal than the stolen Kri, did not do so. Instead, it protected him. It offered a sense of peace greater than the mysterious sensation he once experienced at the altar of the Sun God.
It wasn't because Jin had any special power related to the Sun God. Jin was simply giving him hope. The hope that he could continue the fight to the end.
Salvation.
Shimat suddenly thought of that word. The words of the Battle King warrior, saying they had been saved by Jin.
'Salvation... comes not from a god, but from a person.'
In that sense, Shimat was being saved at that moment, even though saving his own life and that of his people was still an impossible task.
Just breaking free from long-held and futile delusions and facing the truth was, at times, salvation.
Of course, Jin did not respect Shimat, regardless of his realization. There were too many innocents who had died by their red swords.
Jin had spared him only because Shimat’s blade was now turned towards Lokia instead of himself. Had Shimat made a different decision, Jin would have been the first to obliterate him.
"Thank you, Jin Runcandel. Though it's impossible for us to become comrades, I will do my best for my people until the end. I owe it to you for giving me the chance to fight for my people."
Shimat took a deep breath. He was accepting the blue thunder energy that enveloped him.
His heart of light had once accepted this blue energy.

It was on the day he was wrongly accused and exiled from Critil, when he accidentally encountered Eltiot. Even then, Eltiot, already a giant, had tried to welcome him to Blue Plutonian, but Shimat betrayed him, believing it to be the path of the Red Plutonian.
"And shamelessly, I have one more request. Tell the Elder of the Blue Wind Emperor... I'm sorry. Thanks to you, I realized how great the favor he did for me was."
Shimat's heart of light began to take on a purple hue.
Harmony, the trait he learned from Eltiot and had been denying all this time. The truth he had dismissed as an illusion concocted by the weak and non-cruel to hide themselves.
Tetallon.
Shimat threw away the sword imbued with the power of the Sun God. To realize the newly awakened truth, that sword contained too many outdated things.
Instead, Shimat carefully formed a new purple sword using the thunder energy. The solid blade, seemingly unclouded by anything, gleamed brightly in his hand.
Shimat was so intoxicated with this sensation that he lost track of time.
More than 30 minutes had passed since he accepted the blue thunder energy and discarded Tetallon. During this time, countless exchanges had taken place between Jin, his companions, and Lokia.
Jin was no longer standing guard over Lafrarosa. In his place, Murakan and the Battle Kings were protecting it.
Sigmund, ignoring the four air fortresses, extended only towards Kri.
The tremendously huge hull of Kri meant that once its protective shield was penetrated, all of it became a target.
However, Kri was not just a massive air fortress. It was a war machine that applied the essence of the Red Plutonian’s technology to its limits, moving as if it were not a ship but a void space.
When a sword struck its armor, suddenly that part would distort and disappear. If a sword energy capable of covering a part of the hull was shot, exactly the area it touched would become transparent.
As a result, Jin's sword strikes kept hitting empty air. No matter how fierce the sword, it couldn't cut its target if it didn't make contact.
But Jin wasn't feeling frustrated. Nor did Lokia think Jin's attacks were in vain.
Jin was simply finding a way. A way to reach Lokia without having to completely destroy Kri.
Destroying Kri came after extinguishing Lokia's spirit form. From that spirit form, Jin needed to find clues to the real location of Lokia.
On the opposite side, Shimat's purple thunder energy was piercing through Kri. He too, like Jin, was searching for Lokia's spirit form. Only by killing her could his people be released from chaos.
'As expected, it wasn't inside the fortress.'
Jin was the first to pinpoint the location of the spirit.
Sigmund had already passed through the entirety of Kri. Since the sword had not caught anything, Lokia's spirit form had to be outside.
The space where Lokia had been hiding until now was behind the passage of Lafrarosa, in a pit. And there, a main cannon separated from Kri was also made transparent.
As Jin turned around, Lokia smiled at him. If the cannon fired, it could be blocked. But in doing so, not only Murakan but also the Battle Kings would inevitably be injured.
However, the cannon did not fire.
"Even one who was among the Ten Knights spends time on such trivial play. Or have you lost your touch because it's been a long time since you've personally engaged in battle?"
Originally, Kri moved based on dark energy. To fully exploit its performance, Shimat's heart of light, their Battle God, was also necessary.

But now, the largest part of Kri's energy was the chaotic energy manipulated by Lokia. And Jin, while locating Lokia's position, was gradually tying up her chaotic energy to prevent her from carrying out such schemes.

"It would be better for you to try and protect Kri now, Lokia. It seems you've forgotten, but without this ship, you can't threaten my brothers at all. The one who has something to protect now is not just me……"
Jin's sword was again directed towards Kri.
